clue.text: Possible reason for mass reduction of penny pincher's claim for reparation

indicators.note: a claim put up for repair is to be rebuilt, so its letters and those beside it are reassembled

parts.note: penny cut down to its abbreviation, the single letter p
the possessive is kept as a letter s here, joining the anagram pool

explanation.surface: A miser, cutting costs to the bone, puts in a claim for compensation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mass reduction' looks like one phrase, but the definition stops at 'mass'; the possessive S of pincher's counts as a letter in the pool.
explanation.definitionFit: Ernst Mach's hypothesis holds that a body's inertia, and so its mass, arises from all the distant matter in the universe.

clue.text: Has German Earl, breaking and entering of course, over a barrel

indicators.note: the scrambled group goes into the turned interjection, as a burglar enters a house
in a down clue 'over' means the word is flipped, read bottom to top

parts.note: D'oh, Homer Simpson's exclamation, is a mocking 'of course!'

indicators.note: the letters are broken up and rearranged

parts.note: has stays as written, then G is the abbreviation for German and E for Earl

explanation.surface: A German nobleman caught housebreaking finds himself over a barrel, in trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over a barrel' reads as an idiom meaning in trouble, but 'over' works alone as the turning signal in a down clue. D'oh, Homer Simpson's exclamation, stands for 'of course!'.
explanation.definitionFit: A hogshead is a large cask, traditionally holding around fifty gallons of ale or wine.

clue.text: Boyfriend and girlfriend want sex with perverted writer

parts.note: 'it' is a familiar euphemism for sex

indicators.note: turned the wrong way round, so this word is read backwards

parts.note: the setter, the writer of the clue, calls himself 'me'

explanation.surface: A couple are interested only in sex with a writer of dubious tastes.
explanation.walkthrough: The writer is the setter, so ME; 'perverted' turns it into EM.
explanation.definitionFit: Gossip calls a romantic couple seen together an item.

clue.text: Exquisite result from Talk Sport?

indicators.note: talkSPORT is a British sports radio station, so the scoreline is heard spoken over the airwaves

parts.note: a two-all draw, read out as 'two-two'

explanation.surface: A sports radio station broadcasts a lovely scoreline.
explanation.walkthrough: talkSPORT is a British sports radio station; a score of two goals each, announced on it, sounds like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: 'Too too' is a dated affected expression meaning excessively refined or delightful.

clue.text: Part of cycle cut short rehabilitation of the unwell

indicators.note: the letters are restored to a new working order, so they are rearranged
the last letter of 'unwell' is lopped off

explanation.surface: Part of the cycle of treatment was curtailed for convalescing patients.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cut short' takes the last L off UNWELL; THE plus UNWEL is then rearranged by 'rehabilitation of'. 'cycle' hints at therapy but means a bicycle.
explanation.definitionFit: A wheel nut fastens a wheel to its hub, a small component of a bicycle or car.

clue.text: Marker of papers has bundle of notes reportedly put away

indicators.note: the pieces are to be said aloud, giving a phrase that sounds the same

parts.words: Marker of papers has bundle of notes
parts.note: ink marks paper, and it 'has' a wad, a roll of banknotes: ink wad

explanation.surface: An examiner of papers has a pile of cash quietly stashed away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Marker of papers' suggests a teacher, but it is ink. 'Quod' is old British slang for prison.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone in prison, slangily 'in quod', has been locked up, or put away.

clue.text: In seated position, reject left hospital opening as the possessor of 12, perhaps, 24 and 1

indicators.note: everything before it is placed inside the little word that follows

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: the next pieces sit inside the word for position

parts.note: a pose is a position held

indicators.note: rejecting throws a word back, so it is read in reverse

parts.note: port is the nautical word for left

indicators.note: the opening letter of hospital

explanation.surface: A patient told to sit up refuses to leave by the hospital doorway.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reject' makes TROP; 'seated' puts it with H inside a word for position, and 'In' puts all that inside the clue's 'as'. 'opening' is a first letter, not part of the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Singular possessives such as Mother's, Peter's and Mach's are written with an apostrophe then S.

clue.text: More than one blow for radio's "Coxy" after punching namesakes

indicators.note: the plural goes into the single name, as a fist goes into something

parts.note: other people called Sara
Sara Cox is a BBC radio DJ, nicknamed Coxy

explanation.surface: A radio DJ throws punches at women who share her name.
explanation.walkthrough: Sara Cox is a well-known BBC Radio presenter. A sasarara is a dialect word for a severe scolding or blow.
explanation.definitionFit: A sasarara (a form of 'certiorari') is a severe beating or reprimand; plural, several such blows.

clue.text: /27. At a single fell swoop, your setter's left unconscious

indicators.note: the setter has left, so that letter is removed

parts.note: 'in one go' means all at once
the setter refers to himself as I

explanation.surface: A setter knocked out in one swift blow is left senseless.
explanation.walkthrough: 'your setter's left' reads as possession, but 's is 'has': I has left IN ONE GO.
explanation.definitionFit: Philosophers use the term for everything outside the conscious self, the not-self.

clue.text: Indy, as renowned fleetingly?

indicators.note: fame that passes quickly is unstable, so the letters shift

explanation.surface: The Independent newspaper enjoys only brief fame.
explanation.walkthrough: The Indy is the Independent, the paper the puzzle ran in; the whole clue is both definition and anagram fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: A short-lived sensation that is quickly forgotten, like a newspaper's passing celebrity.

clue.text: /26. A dog is in possession of 18 toes: as for the human race?

definitions.text: A dog is in possession of 18 toes: as for the human
definitions.meaning: while a dog owns eighteen toes, a person, in jokey grammar, owns two fives' worth

explanation.surface: A canine anatomy fact sets a dog's toe count against a person's.
explanation.walkthrough: Split as two words, the answer completes 'the human ...' in deliberately bad grammar; as one word it means race.
explanation.definitionFit: To race somewhere is to hurry or speed up, which this verb means.

clue.text: Gordon's thermos?

parts.note: the word thermos is what you get from wrecking the letters of mothers: the ruin of mothers

explanation.surface: A flask belonging to someone named Gordon.
explanation.walkthrough: A reverse clue: read the answer as wordplay, 'ruin' of MOTHERS, and the result is THERMOS. Gordon's is a well-known British gin brand.
explanation.definitionFit: Gin has been nicknamed this since the gin-soaked squalor of eighteenth-century London, and Gordon's is a brand of it.

clue.text: Old acquaintance of Elliott attracts contempt in a restful literary area

indicators.note: the pieces go inside the word for 'a'

parts.note: per means 'a', as in five pounds a head
E.T., the alien befriended by the boy Elliott in the Spielberg film
scorn means contempt

explanation.surface: A former friend of Elliott is scorned in a quiet bookish nook.
explanation.walkthrough: Elliott is the boy in the film E.T., not T.S. Eliot; 'a' is PER, as in 'per head'.
explanation.definitionFit: This part of Westminster Abbey is where many great poets are buried or memorialised, so they rest there.

clue.text: They are true facts about League battles

indicators.note: the outer word goes around the inner pieces

parts.note: stats, short for statistics, are facts
war is a series of battles

explanation.surface: Accurate figures concern football league battles.
explanation.walkthrough: 'true facts' reads as one phrase, but the definition ends at 'true'.
explanation.definitionFit: Loyal, dependable supporters, those who stay faithful, are called stalwarts.

clue.text: /20. Oxon community executed business on time

parts.note: did means carried out, executed
Co is short for company, a business

explanation.surface: An Oxfordshire village carried out its business punctually.
explanation.walkthrough: Oxon is the abbreviation for Oxfordshire; Didcot is a railway town there.
explanation.definitionFit: Didcot is a town in Oxfordshire, a community within the county.

clue.text: State of mind I analyse

indicators.note: the answer is formed of letters within the following words

explanation.surface: A psychoanalyst describes examining a state of mind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'State of mind' reads as one phrase, but the definition is 'State' alone.
explanation.definitionFit: Indiana is one of the fifty states of the USA.

clue.text: Opposition bishop's stake covers East London rap

indicators.note: the stake wraps around the music

parts.note: an ante is a poker stake

indicators.note: Cockneys from East London drop their aitches, so both H letters go

parts.note: rap is a form of hip hop

explanation.surface: A bishop's wager encompasses East End rap music.
explanation.walkthrough: 'East London' drops both H letters from HIPHOP, giving IPOP, as a Cockney speaker would.
explanation.definitionFit: An antipope is a rival claimant set up against the lawful Pope, who is the Bishop of Rome.

clue.text: Like Hacker, maybe, wearing Tory hat?

indicators.note: something worn out is battered out of shape, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Jim Hacker, the Yes Minister politician, sports a Conservative hat.
explanation.walkthrough: Jim Hacker is the minister in the British sitcom Yes Minister, but here a hacker is one with a hacking cough.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone with a hacking cough sounds rough and husky, coming from deep in the gullet.

clue.text: Where Budgie put down songs aimed for Number One

parts.note: airs are tunes or songs
something that tops the list is the best

explanation.surface: A budgie sang songs hoping to reach the top of the charts.
explanation.walkthrough: Budgie is the Little Helicopter of a children's book series, so his landing places are for helicopters, not a pet bird.
explanation.definitionFit: Helicopter landing places are called airstops, and Budgie is a cartoon helicopter.

clue.text: See 15
Pointedly design some military entertainment

definitions.meaning: to mark the skin with a picture using needle points
a military display of marching and music, such as the Edinburgh one

explanation.definitionFit: The word covers both inking skin with needles and an evening drum signal that grew into a military show.

clue.text: In the company of shipmates, getting hazy quaffing strong Fuller's ale, a heady concoction

indicators.note: drinking down, so the ale goes inside the jumbled letters
becoming blurred, so the letters lose their order

parts.note: with means in the company of
a ship's crew
ESB, Extra Special Bitter, is a strong beer brewed by Fuller's of London

explanation.surface: Drinking strong beer among fellow sailors leaves everyone fuzzy-headed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'getting hazy' scrambles the phrase for being among shipmates, and 'quaffing' swallows the beer midway. ESB is Extra Special Bitter, a strong London ale.
explanation.definitionFit: A witches' brew is a potent, fearsome mixture, like the cauldron stew in Macbeth.

clue.text: Underneath one's table, concealed upright

indicators.note: the answer is tucked away inside these words

explanation.surface: Something is hidden under someone's table.
explanation.definitionFit: An upright person is honourable and truthful.

clue.text: Writer — in respect of a sort — appended tab, not payment for 17

indicators.note: the last piece is added on at the end
the writer goes inside the rearranged word
the word is sorted into a different order

parts.note: a pen is a writing instrument
a tab is a pill, and E is ecstasy

explanation.surface: A writer, in a manner of speaking, tacks on a bill he will not pay.
explanation.walkthrough: 'of a sort' makes PETERSC; 'appended' adds E, an ecstasy tablet. 'not' is a link here. 17 is ANTIPOPE, so the payment goes to a pope.
explanation.definitionFit: Peter's Pence is an annual levy or offering paid to the Pope, the successor of St Peter.

clue.text: Make long year short

indicators.note: the word for long falls short of one letter

parts.note: to long is to yearn

explanation.surface: Turn a long year into a short one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'short' removes Y (year) from YEARN.
explanation.definitionFit: To make money is to gain it by work, a synonym in the sense of income.

indicators.note: the letters are rearranged into order
